limitations: F1 — Counterevidence: Nontrivial centralizer proof starts by explicitly choosing u!=id; its cancellation is valid. Cor5.3 uses a nontrivial cyclic Ga for u!=id.
F2 — Counterevidence: Generic stabilizers are still trivial in this exact example.
F3 — Counterevidence: p19 proves algebraicity and same dimension; Theorem8.5(c) later uses generalized roots.
F4 — Counterevidence: Nonnegative exponent choices outside the same forbidden sets exist.
F5 — Counterevidence: For primes not dividing the finite component group order the claimed rank is correct.
F6 — Counterevidence: Already H and theta(H) algebraic on p25; already Y toric in p27 first case.
F7 — Counterevidence: Actual finite-kernel application requires0<r<n. n1 impossible; n2 r1 targetGL1(Z) finite, so infinite source cannot have finite kernel.
Not performed: Complete proofs of CRX/GP93/Borel-Tits/root-weight reconstruction/Losev/Cantat-Xie/Margulis external inputs.
Not performed: Full independent classification of projective examples.

proposition.claim:
Central classification includes trivial groups

A maximum-dimensional component of E dominates the base

Arbitrary-dimensional generalized root maps to an ordinary root of same dimension

Selected integer exponents give regular replicas; every nonempty forbidden lattice has rank m-1

p-torsion rank of diagonalizable D equals dimD for every prime

Theorem8.5 applies to H=DU and to a torus source

All n satisfy dimZ>=n for finite-index SLn(Z) embeddings
